title: Baseball Game
summary: You keep a score log that starts empty and get a list of string commands `ops`. An integer command, possibly negative, records that score. `"+"` records a new score equal to the sum of the last two, `"D"` records double the most recent score, and `"C"` cancels the most recent score, deleting it from the log for good. Return the sum of the scores left in the log at the end.

examples.explanation: The log grows to [4, -2, 2, 4]; "C" deletes the last 4, then 7 is recorded: 4 - 2 + 2 + 7 = 11.
"C" deletes 9, so "+" adds the two scores that are now the most recent: 2 + 5 = 7, and 2 + 5 + 7 = 14.

constraints: Each command is "+", "D", "C" or an integer from −3·10⁴ to 3·10⁴ written as a string
"+" always finds at least two scores in the log, and "D" and "C" at least one
Every score and the final sum fit in a 32-bit signed integer

approaches.twist: Push each new score, pop the top on "C", and read the top one or two scores for "D" and "+".
Never delete: mark cancelled scores, and scan back past them to find the latest live scores for "+", "D" and "C".
approaches.note: Works, but cancelled scores pile up and a scan back may cross all of them, so it takes O(n²) time. The target is O(n).

signals.meaning: Every command works on the newest scores, and the newest score is always on top of a stack, where stack[-1] reads it.
Read the top two scores, stack[-1] and stack[-2], without popping them: both stay in the log.
An undo. Pop the newest score, and the one before it becomes the newest again, ready for the next "+" or "D".

constraintReading: len(ops) is at most 1000, so even O(n²) would finish quickly. The O(n) target asks for O(1) work per command: a push, a pop, or a look at the top one or two scores. The log may keep every score, so the space is O(n).

related.relation: Also pushes numbers and combines the top two, but an operator pops both operands and pushes one result, while "+" here keeps both scores.
